rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the mountain as torn out and raised, comparing the wording to the raising of Sinai over the Israelites.
rows.anchor: قلعناه ورفعناه ، كقوله : ورفعنا فوقهم الطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also describes shaking a waterskin to dislodge its butter.
rows.anchor: ومنه : نتق السقاء ، إذا نفضه ليقتلع الزبدة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ẓullah is anything that provides shade, such as a roof or cloud.
rows.anchor: والظلة : كل ما أظلك من سقيفة أو سحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with ṭāʾ derives the word from something looming over another.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالطاء ، من أطل عليه إذا أشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites had refused the Torah as burdensome, so God raised a parasang-square mountain over their camp and threatened to drop it unless they accepted it.
rows.anchor: فرفع الله الطور على رؤسهم مقدار عسكرهم ، وكان فرسخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fear, each Israelite prostrated on the left brow while watching the mountain with the right eye; this explains their reported prostration custom and claim that it lifted punishment.
rows.anchor: خر كل رجل منهم ساجدا على حاجبه الأيسر وهو ينظر بعينه اليمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses spread the inscribed tablets, mountains, trees, and stones shook; Jews reading Torah are likewise said to sway and nod.
rows.anchor: ولما نشر موسى الألواح وفيها كتاب الله . لم يبق جبل ولا شجر ولا حجر إلا اهتز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to take what was given is elliptical for God saying, 'Take what We gave you,' namely the Book.
rows.anchor: على إرادة القول . أي : وقلنا خذوا ما آتيناكم ، أو قائلين : خذوا ما آتيناكم من الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the Book means resolving to bear its hardships and obligations.
rows.anchor: وعزم على احتمال مشاقه وتكاليفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering what the Book contains can mean keeping its commands and prohibitions, or recalling its promise of great reward as an incentive.
rows.anchor: من الأوامر والنواهي ولا تنسوه ، أو اذكروا ما فيه من التعريض للثواب العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, taking it firmly means bearing the mighty sign if able, like the challenge to pass beyond the heavens; remembering it means recalling its proof of power and warning.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : خذوا ما آتيناكم من الآية العظيمة بقوة إن كنتم تطيقونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that they become mindful of their present conduct.
rows.anchor: من الدلالة على القدرة الباهرة والإنذار

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads 'and remember' (وتذكروا); another reading gives واذكروا with the same sense.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( وتذكروا ) وقرىء : ( واذكروا ) ، بمعنى وتذكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'From their backs' is a partitive apposition to 'the children of Adam.'
rows.anchor: بدل من بني آدم بدل البعض من الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking their descendants from their backs means bringing offspring out of their loins and making them testify about themselves.
rows.anchor: إخراجهم من أصلابهم نسلا وإشهادهم على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dialogue is representational: God established proofs of His lordship and oneness, which the intellects and insights He built into people recognize.
rows.anchor: قوله : { ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا } من باب التمثيل والتخييلا ومعنى ذلك أنه نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reason and insight distinguish error from guidance, so it is as though God made them testify and ask whether He is their Lord.
rows.anchor: وشهدت بها عقولهم وبصائرهم التي ركبها فيهم وجعلها مميزة بين الضلالة والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imagined answer is an affirmation that God is their Lord and that they acknowledge His oneness.
rows.anchor: وكأنهم قالوا : بلى أنت ربنا ، شهدنا على أنفسنا وأقررنا بوحدانيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such representational speech is common in divine, Prophetic, and Arabic expression; the Qur'an's address to heaven and earth is another example.
rows.anchor: وباب التمثيل واسع في كلام الله تعالى ورسوله عليه الصلاة السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic image of bodily parts speaking likewise represents meaning rather than actual speech.
rows.anchor: إذ قالت الأنساع للبطن الحق قالت له ريح الصبا قرقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of establishing rational proofs is to prevent people from claiming on Judgment Day that they were unaware of them.
rows.anchor: أي فعلنا ذلك من نصب الأدلة الشاهدة على صحتها العقول ، كراهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same proofs prevent the excuse that people merely followed their polytheist fathers; neither descendants nor their ancestors have an excuse to ignore the evidence for oneness.
rows.anchor: فلا عذر لهم في الإعراض عنه والإقبال على التقليد والاقتداء بالآباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies Adam's forefathers here as Jewish ancestors who called ʿUzayr God's son, and their descendants as contemporaries of the Messenger who followed them.
rows.anchor: عنى ببني آدم : أسلاف اليهود الذين أشركوا بالله ، حيث قالوا : عزير ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context identifies the descendants as the Jews and their ancestors as polytheists; the cited surrounding passages concern the same community.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أنها في اليهود : الآيات التي عطفت عليها هي ، والتي عطفت عليها وهي على نمطها وأسلوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants' claim that wrongdoers caused their destruction refers to ancestors who established polytheism and left it as a precedent.
rows.anchor: أي كانوا السبب في شركنا ؛ لتأسيسهم الشرك ، وتقدمهم فيه ، وتركه سنة لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God details the signs with such clarity so that they may return from their polytheism.
rows.anchor: وإرادة أن يرجعوا عن شركهم نفصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the singular ذُرِّيَّتَهُ; another reads أن يقولوا with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ذريتهم ) على التوحيد . وأن يقولوا : بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He matches 'guided' to the singular surface form, while 'those are the losers' follows the plural meaning.
rows.anchor: حمل على اللفظ . و { فأولئك هم الخاسرون } حمل على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many jinn and humans destined for Hell are those whose hearts are sealed and whom God knows will receive no special divine aid.
rows.anchor: هم المطبوع على قلوبهم الذين علم الله أنه لا لطف لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fail to direct their minds to truth, inspect creation reflectively, or listen to God's signs with attention, as if deprived of the faculties' proper use.
rows.anchor: لا يلقون أذهانهم إلى معرفة الحق ، ولا ينظرون بأعينهم إلى ما خلق الله نظر اعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeply rooted disbelief and obstinacy, and their consistently hellish deeds, make them seem created for Hell by way of describing their entrenched qualification for it.
rows.anchor: لإعراقهم في الكفر وشدة شكائمهم فيه ، وأنه لا يأتي منهم إلا أفعال أهل النار مخلوقين للنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A letter from ʿUmar to Khālid b. al-Walīd says that people in Syria prepared a wine-mixed ointment for him and calls the Mughīra family born for Hell; the idiom describes deep rootedness in a trait.
rows.anchor: ومنـه كتاب عمر رضي الله عنه إلى خالد بن الوليد : بلغني أن أهل الشام اتخذوا لك دلوكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He applies the description especially to Jews who denied the Messenger despite knowing he was the promised prophet, among those from whom faith scarcely comes.
rows.anchor: والمراد وصف حال اليهود في عظم ما أقدموا عليه من تكذيب رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble cattle because they lack understanding, reflective sight, and attentive hearing; they are still further astray.
rows.anchor: في عدم الفقه والنظر للاعتبار والاستماع للتدبر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Cattle see their benefits and harms and follow some of what they perceive, whereas most of these people knowingly persist in defiance and rush toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الأنعام تبصر منافعها ومضارها فتلزم بعض ما تبصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's names are the most beautiful because they express good meanings such as glorification and sanctification, and He should be invoked by them.
rows.anchor: التي هي أحسن الأسماء ؛ لأنها تدل على معان حسنة من تمجيد وتقديس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deviate in the names either call God by impermissible labels, as ignorant Bedouins do, or refuse one of His beautiful names, such as al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: كما سمعنا البدو يقولون بجهلهم : يا أبا المكارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse means God's beautiful attributes: affirm justice, goodness, and beneficence and deny creaturely likeness; leave those who attribute evil acts or likeness to Him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : ولله الأوصاف الحسنى ، وهي الوصف بالعدل والخير والإحسان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies deviation in the names with calling idols gods and deriving al-Lāt from Allah and al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إلحادهم في أسمائه : تسميتهم الأصنام آلهة ، واشتقاقهم اللات من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional 'if you saw' treats the present as past, just as in transfers the past into the future.
rows.anchor: ترد المضارع إلى معنى الماضي ؛ كما ترد ( إن ) الماضي إلى معنى الاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses idh as an accusative time adverb; yutawaffā is read with yāʾ or tāʾ, with the angels as its nominative subject and 'striking' as their circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: و { إذ } نصب على الظرف وقرىء : ( يتوفى ) بالياء والتاء و { الملائكة } رفعها بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God is the implicit subject of yutawaffā, while 'the angels' begins the clause and 'striking' is its predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في { يتوفى } ضمير الله عز وجل ، و { الملائكة } مرفوعة بالابتداء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses 'their backsides' as their anuses; they are singled out because striking them is especially humiliating and punitive.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : وأدبارهم : استاههم ، ولكن الله كريم يكنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports hearing that in China an adulterer was impaled and then struck once on the buttock with a heavy handled iron disk, freezing in place.
rows.anchor: وبلغني عن أهل الصين أن عقوبة الزاني عندهم أن يصبر ، ثم يعطي الرجل القوي البطش

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the angels strike whatever part faces them and whatever part is behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يضربون ما أقبل منهم وما أدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Taste the burning torment' is either speech by the angels, an advance notice of Hell's torment, or words addressed to them on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: معطوف على { يضربون } على إرادة القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to 'if you saw' is that one would see a dreadful, terrible scene.
rows.anchor: وجواب { لو } محذوف : أي لرأيت أمرا فظيعا منكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'That is because...' may be God's speech or the angels' speech; the punishment rests on disbelief and sins, and on God's justice toward His servants.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك العذاب بسببين : بسبب كفركم ومعاصيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains God's not being unjust as the justice of punishing disbelievers just as He rewards believers; alternatively, ẓallām is intensive for servants or for the severity of punishment, which would otherwise be grossly unjust.
rows.anchor: لأن تعذيب الكفار من العدل كإثابة المؤمنين . وقيل : ظلام للتكثير لأجل العبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of 'do they not see' varies between yāʾ and tāʾ; the trials may be illness, drought, and other divine tests that do not make the hypocrites repent or reflect.
rows.anchor: بالمرض والقحط وغيرهما من بلاء الله ثم لا ينتهون ولا يتوبون عن نفاقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are tested in jihad alongside the Messenger, witnessing his support and victory, yet still fail to learn.
rows.anchor: أو يبتلون في الجهاد مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويعاينون أمره وما ينزل الله عليه من نصرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Satan tempts them to lie and break their covenants with the Messenger, who then kills and punishes them, but they remain undeterred.
rows.anchor: أو يفتنهم الشيطان فيكذبون وينقضون العهود مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' glances at one another may mock the revelation and ask whether any Muslim sees them before they slip away, unable to bear listening and fearing exposure through laughter.
rows.anchor: تغامزوا بالعيون إنكارا للوحي وسخرية به قائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they exchange glances to plan a furtive escape and ask whether anyone can see them.
rows.anchor: أو ترامقوا يتشاورون في تدبير الخروج والانسلال لواذا يقولون : هل يراكم من أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's turning of their hearts is a prayer against them for abandonment, turning them away from the believers' inward openness because they do not understand reflectively.
rows.anchor: دعاء عليهم بالخذلان وبصرف قلوبهم عما في قلوب أهل الإيمان من الانشراح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'From yourselves' means from your own kind and lineage: an Arab Qurayshite like you.
rows.anchor: من جنسكم ومن نسبكم عربي قرشي مثلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because he is one of you, your hardship and painful encounters distress him, and he fears your bad end and punishment.
rows.anchor: شديد عليه شاق لكونه بعضا منكم عنتكم ولقاؤكم المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is eager that none of you abandon following him and attaining happiness through the true religion he brought; he is compassionate to believers from among you and others.
rows.anchor: حتى لا يخرج أحد منكم عن اتباعه والاستسعاد بدين الحق الذي جاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading takes 'from your souls' to mean from your noblest and most excellent; it is attributed to the Prophet, Fāṭima, and ʿĀʾisha.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( من أنفسكم ) أي من أشرفكم وأفضلكم . وقيل : هي قراءة رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that God joined two of His names for no one besides the Messenger in describing him as compassionate and merciful.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لم يجمع الله اسمين من أسمائه لأحد غير رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away from faith and oppose the Messenger, he should seek God's help and entrust matters to Him, for God suffices and supports him against them.
rows.anchor: فإن أعرضوا عن الإيمان بك وناصبوك فاستعن وفوض إليه ، فهو كافيك معرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has al-ʿaẓīm in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { العظيم } بالرفع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no one can measure the size of the Throne.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : العرش لا يقدر أحد قدره

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb says the last verse revealed was 'A messenger has come to you from among yourselves.'
rows.anchor: وعن أبي ابن كعب : آخر آية نزلت : { لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم }

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the Qur'an came down verse by verse and letter by letter, except Sūrat Barāʾa and Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad, which came with seventy thousand ranks of angels.
rows.anchor:
عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :
( 504 ) ( ما نزل علي القرآن إلا آية آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not hoping to meet God can mean not expecting it at all because heedlessness and desire for immediate pleasures prevent attention to realities; alternatively, it means not hoping for a favorable meeting or not fearing the bad meeting one should fear.
rows.anchor: لا يتوقعونه أصلا ، ولا يخطرونه ببالهم لغفلتهم المستولية عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They prefer worldly life to the afterlife, choosing the little and perishable over the abundant and lasting, as also stated in the rebuke in 9:38.
rows.anchor: وآثروا القليل الفاني على الكثير الباقي ، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being settled in worldly life means resting there as though they will never be displaced, building strongly and hoping far ahead.
rows.anchor: وسكنوا فيها سكون من لا يزعج عنها ، فبنوا شديدا وأملوا بعيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause beginning with ḥattā ends the account of Noah building the ark: he built it until the appointed time arrived.
rows.anchor: هي التي يبتدأ بعدها الكلام ، دخلت على الجملة من الشرط والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intervening mockery is a circumstantial clause: he built while groups of his people passed and mocked him.
rows.anchor: هو حال من يصنع ، كأنه قال : يصنعها والحال أنه كلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers two parses for kullamā: either 'they mocked' answers it and 'he said' resumes an implied question, or 'they mocked' is an apposition to 'passed' or an adjective of 'group,' with 'he said' as the answer.
rows.anchor: إما أن تجعل ( سخروا ) جوابا و ( قال ) استئنافا ، على تقدير سؤال سائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Your family' and 'whoever believed' are coordinated with 'two of each': carry the family and other believers too.
rows.anchor: عطف على اثنين ، وكذلك { ومن ءامن } يعني : واحمل أهلك والمؤمنين من غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in Noah's family under the prior decree are excluded because God knew they would choose disbelief, not because He decreed or willed disbelief; God is exalted above that.
rows.anchor: وما سبق عليه القول بذلك إلا للعلم بأنه يختار الكفر ، لا لتقديره عليه وإرادته به تعالى الله عن ذلك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the excluded family members as Noah's son and wife.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : أراد ابنه وامرأته

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report counts eight aboard: Noah, his family, his three sons, and their wives.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال :
( 525 ) ( كانوا ثمانية : نوح وأهله ، وبنوه الثلاثة ، ونساؤهم )

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muḥammad b. Isḥāq says they numbered ten, five men and five women.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن إسحاق : كانوا عشرة : خمسة رجال وخمس نسوة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says seventy-two men and women; it also names Noah's sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth and their wives, giving a total of seventy-eight, half male and half female.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانوا اثنين وسبعين رجلا وامرأة ، وأولاد نوح : سام وحام ويافث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construction joins 'in God's name' to 'ride' as a circumstantial phrase: they ride naming God or saying the basmala at sailing and anchoring, whether understood as times or verbal nouns with an omitted time noun.
rows.anchor: أن يتصل { بسم الله } باركبوا حالا من الواو ، بمعنى : اركبوا فيها مسمين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the two words refer to places of setting out and anchoring, governed by the verbal meaning of the basmala or by an implied act of saying.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد مكانا الإجراء والإرساء ، وانتصابهما بما في { بسم الله } من معنى الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second construction makes 'In God's name is its sailing and anchoring' a complete subject-predicate sentence.
rows.anchor: أن يكون { بسم الله مجراها ومرساها } جملة من مبتدأ وخبر مقتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is related that whenever Noah wanted the ark to sail or settle, he said 'In God's name,' and it then sailed or anchored.
rows.anchor: يروى أنه كان إذا أراد أن تجري قال : بسم الله فجرت ، وإذا أراد أن ترسو قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'clear authority' either means that Moses' signs prove his prophethood or specifically means the staff, the most remarkable sign.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أن يراد أن هذه الآيات فيها سلطان مبين لموسى على صدق نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Pharaoh's command unguided rebukes his followers: he claimed divinity despite being human, practiced tyranny and evil, yet they followed his manifest misguidance.
rows.anchor: تجهيل لمتبعيه حيث شايعوه على أمره ، وهو ضلال مبين لا يخفى على من فيه أدنى مسكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had witnessed Moses' signs and knew he carried guidance and truth, yet chose a leader whose command had no guidance.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنهم عاينوا الآيات والسلطان المبين في أمر موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'His command was not rightly guided' may instead mean that it was not good or commendable in its outcome.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بقوله : { وما أمر فرعون برشيد } وما أمره بصالح حميد العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh leads his people to the Fire as he had served as their exemplar in error; this may explain why his command was not commendable.
rows.anchor: { يقدم قومه } أي كما كان قدوة لهم في الضلال كذلك يتقدمهم إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rashīd is used for anything praised and approved, while ghayy is used for anything blameworthy and detested.
rows.anchor: والرشد مستعمل في كل ما يحمد ويرتضى ، كما استعمل الغي في كل ما يذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root q-d-m means to precede, as in the front of a saddle, the vanguard of an army, and related forms.
rows.anchor: وأقدم بمعنى تقدم . ومنه مقدم العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense 'he brought them' marks an existing, certain outcome: he will inevitably lead them into the Fire.
rows.anchor: لأن الماضي يدل على أمر موجود مقطوع به ، فكأنه قيل : يقدمهم فيوردهم النار لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are likened to a caravan arriving at water and Pharaoh to the one who goes ahead; calling the Fire a bad watering place reverses water's purpose of quenching thirst and cooling hearts.
rows.anchor: شبه بالفارط الذي يتقدم الواردة إلى الماء . وشبه أتباعه بالواردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are followed by a curse in this world and the next; the worldly curse supports and extends their punishment, reinforced by the afterlife curse.
rows.anchor: أي يلعنون في الدنيا ، ويلعنون في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means how bad is the gift that was given.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بئس العطاء المعطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing occurring in the heavens or earth is hidden from God, so your deeds are not hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: لا تخفى عليه خافية مما يجري فيهما ، فلا تخفى عليه أعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All affairs return to God, so their affairs and the Messenger's will return to Him and He will avenge the Messenger against them.
rows.anchor: فلا بد أن يرجع إليه أمرهم وأمرك ، فينتقم لك منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God and rely on Him because He is sufficient and protective.
rows.anchor: { فاعبده وتوكل عليه } فإنه كافيك وكافلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading uses second-person plural taʿmalūn, addressing both the addressee and the others by giving precedence to the direct addressee.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( تعملون ) بالتاء : أي أنت وهم على تغليب المخاطب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report promises ten good deeds for each person who believed or disbelieved in Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb, Lot, Abraham, and Moses to whoever recites Sūrat Hūd, and says the reciter will be among the fortunate on Judgment Day, God willing.
rows.anchor:
عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :
( 537 ) من قرأ سورة هود أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand for a sign is astonishing because the Messenger had many unparalleled signs, with the Qur'an alone sufficient; denying them as though no sign came merits rebuke.
rows.anchor: أن الآيات الباهرة المتكاثرة التي أوتيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يؤتها نبي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leads astray those fixed in disbelief and obstinate, who would not be guided even if every sign were sent; He guides those of the opposite character who turn toward truth.
rows.anchor: إن الله يضل من يشاء ممن كان على صفتكم من التصميم وشدة الشكيمة في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anāba literally means entering the turn or course of goodness.
rows.anchor: وحقيقته دخل في نوبة الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses 'those who disbelieved' as apposition to 'who turns back.'
rows.anchor: { الذين كفروا } بدل من { من أناب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts find rest in mentioning God's mercy and forgiveness after fear and distress, or in remembering proofs of His oneness, or in the Qur'an as a clear miracle that settles hearts and confirms certainty.
rows.anchor: بذكر رحمته ومغفرته بعد القلق والاضطراب من خشيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He construes 'those who disbelieved' as the subject and 'blessedness for them' as its predicate.
rows.anchor: { الذين كفروا } مبتدأ ، و { طوبى لهم } خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tūbā is a verbal noun from ṭāba, like bushrā and zulfā; 'tūbā laka' means that you have attained goodness, and it may be parsed in the accusative or nominative, as with parallel expressions.
rows.anchor: وطوبى مصدر من طاب ، كبشرى وزلفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative and accusative readings of 'and a good return' indicate its possible case positions; the lām in 'for them' is explanatory, and wāw in tūbā changes from yāʾ after a ḍamma.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لهم } للبيان مثلها في سقيا لك ، والواو في طوبى منقلبة عن ياء

rows.speaker: مكوزة الأعرابي
rows.claim: Makūza al-Aʿrābī reads ṭībā with kasra to preserve the yāʾ, as in bayḍ and maʿīsha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مكوزة الأعرابي : ( طيبى لهم ) ، فكسر الطاء لتسلم الياء
